pageCache.pageTitle: Blewbury C of E Primary School - SEND and Inclusion
pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion
Our school is a place for all to belong. Through love, we nurture all to grow in their own unique way. We create an environment for all to flourish; to forgive, be resilient and courageous, making difference to our community and the world beyond.
Here at Blewbury School we have an inclusive ethos and we work closely in partnership with children, parents and other agencies to provide the best possible educational outcomes for all our children; putting support in place as early as possible for any child that needs it.
Individual Provision.
All children on the SEND register have an individual Pupil Profile detailing their strengths, barriers to learning, desired outcomes and strategies to support achieving their outcomes. Children and parents/guardians are invited to meetings to review these profiles three times a year. Working in partnership with parents and guardians ensures they know the best way to support learning and achieve the best outcomes for the children. They are encouraged to engage in supporting their child’s learning, for example, by reading with them regularly, working on phonic sounds, or reinforcing speech therapy activities. Provision Maps are put in place and reviewed on a regular cycle, using data and/or observations as evidence of the impact of interventions.
SENDco
Our SEN governor is Lesley Botchway.
The ODST Inclusion Leader is Mrs Challans

pageCache.pageTitle: Blewbury C of E Primary School - Absence procedures
pageCache.text:
Absence procedures
Child Absence & Attendance
At Blewbury School, your child’s attendance is important to us to ensure they achieve their full potential. Did you know that a child who misses school for one day a week will miss the equivalent of two years of schooling, and 90% of children whose absence falls below 85% fail to achieve 5 or more good grades at GCSE and a third of those children do not pass any GCSEs at all? Regular attendance at school really does impact on your child’s future!

pageCache.pageTitle: Blewbury C of E Primary School - Wraparound care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound care
Breakfast Club and After School Fun Club
Our wrap around care – Breakfast and After School Club is led by Mrs Brabner and supported by Miss Rawson and Miss Daley.
If you have any questions about either of our clubs, please phone 01235850411 or email clubs@blewbury.oxon.sch.uk
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club is run daily from 8:00am until the start of the school day and is based in Class 2 (via secure access from the car park).
Cost: £5.50 per pupil per session and includes refreshments.
To make a payment click here or contact the office for information on how to pay using childcare vouchers.
For last minute bookings (less than 24 hours notice) please ring the office directly 01235 850411.
After School Fun Club
Fun Club is run daily from 3.15 pm until 5.45 pm (4.30 pm on a Friday) and is based in Class 2. Charges as follows
To make a payment click here or contact the office for how to pay using childcare vouchers.
For last minute bookings (less than 24 hours notice) please ring the office directly 01235 850411
Terms and conditions
Please read the full terms and conditions for Breakfast and After School Club. You will be asked to agree and sign this document when you book a place for your child(ren).
Breakfast and After School Fun Club Booking Requests
To request a place at our Breakfast Club or After School Fun Club, please use the booking forms below and email: clubs@blewbury.oxon.sch.uk (or drop in to our school office). Please make sure to record your child’s name and any dates required. You will be contacted to confirm you child’s space.

Visits and open days
“Children get off to an excellent start,”
Choosing a primary school for your child is a big decision. Come and visit our wonderful school, tour our fantastic grounds and find out what we have to offer your child.
Please contact Mrs Emma Bealey (school Administrator) to book a tour: 01235 850411, office.3248@blewbury.oxon.sch.uk
Prospective September 2026 Starters
Each year, there are places available for 25 Reception pupils. Come and visit our Ofsted rated ‘outstanding’ setting on our open morning: Saturday 11th October 2025, 10am-12noon.
This is an informal opportunity for your child to visit the reception classroom and outdoor space and for you to meet members of staff and the governing body.
Book a tour on Wednesday 15th or 22nd October, 26th Novemeber or 3rd December by calling our school office on 01235850411.
Tours will be led by the headteacher and offer you an opportunity to see learning in action and ask any questions you may have.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blewbury C of E Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
“Educating the mind, without educating the heart, is no education at all.”
A Broad and Balanced Curriculum
Our curriculum is firmly rooted in the National Curriculum and the Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework (see links below).
We will ensure that all children flourish academically but of paramount importance is that they also learn the skills and knowledge needed to live successful and happy lives, where they are informed and courageous advocates of the things that matter to them.
To find out more, visit our curriculum Intent, Implementation and Impact statements here.
Curriculum Provision
See our EYFS long term plan here See our KS1 long term plan (2-year cycle) here See our KS2 long term (2-year cycle) plan here
Progression
Click on each subject below to find out more about how we teach it at Blewbury.
How we ensure all children access our Curriculum:
All pupils have access to our curriculum regardless of their individual ability, gender, race, culture or social background or any physical or sensory difficulty. Our aim is that all children shine brightly and achieve highly regardless of their background or circumstances.
Children learn and thrive when they are healthy, safe and engaged. To engage all children, we celebrate difference and diversity within our school community. Blewbury School community is predominantly a white British community and therefore we have carefully chosen, within our curriculum, a range of resources, texts, international links, and inspirational people so cultural diversity is promoted and celebrated.
We ensure that gender is represented equally and that inquiry questions, themes and resources appeal to boys and girls, so all children have equal access to our curriculum.
Provision is made to develop the talents of more able pupils in a variety of ways. Through increasingly complex investigative tasks, and open-ended tasks which enable them to tackle more complex issues and understand more difficult concepts.
Pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities are supported so they can succeed in all areas of our curriculum. Our school inclusion co-ordinator works with all staff to ensure barriers to learning, for pupils with additional needs, are fully understood and strategies are in place to help children overcome these barriers and make good progress. See our SEND Policy (link below) for the full range of support offered.
Further Curriculum Information
National Curriculum – Key Stages One and Two Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework 2023 SEND Policy (Located on the Curriculum & Procedures page.)
Want to know more about our curriculum?
If you would like more information about our curriculum, please contact us and we will get back to you as soon as possible.
